content.aiIntroduction: The results collected here were generated with AI assistance and have not been fully verified by a human.
content.shortBio: I am a third-year undergraduate majoring in Mathematics and Applied Mathematics.
content.aiAboutBody:
The design of this interface was inspired by the personal homepage of Jihao Liu, an assistant professor at Peking University.

I began using AI to assist with my mathematical research in mid-August 2026. Recently, I have gradually obtained some results in areas that interest me. However, I am only an undergraduate, and my time and abilities are limited, so I cannot fully digest the results I have generated in a short period. Since I also wish to [large]**adhere to academic standards**[/large], I have set up this page.

I have recently posted a number of papers on Hexagon for the reasons described below. This page presents [highlight]only some of the more important results[/highlight] I have obtained. **I welcome criticism and suggestions from everyone.** These results have not been uploaded to arXiv.

Some of the papers I posted on Hexagon grew out of my own research interests. Others came about in three ways.

1. Some fellow students, knowing that I have experience using AI for mathematics, asked me to test what it could do in other areas of mathematics or to post on their behalf results they had obtained using AI. Examples include [Schmeisser’s Conjecture in Large Degree](https://hexagonmath.org/2611.00162v1), [A Lower Bound for the Filling Area of the Circle](https://hexagonmath.org/2611.00218v2), and [A Counterexample to the Realizability Conjecture for Surface Classes](https://hexagonmath.org/2611.00489v1).

2. Some faculty members reached out to me to express their interest in seeing solutions to major mathematical problems or progress toward them. I shared the results I obtained on those problems. Examples include [Hall polynomials for representation-finite algebras](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00403v1), [Reduction of the Gorenstein symmetry conjecture to finite rings](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00397v2), and [Cartan determinants in finite representation type over arbitrary fields](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00392v2).

3. Some faculty members asked me to use my experience with AI to tackle mathematical problems that had been open for at least ten years.

In my view, **credit should go to those who truly understand and organize the work**, as well as to the AI systems and agents involved, such as Rethlas, Danus, Pharos, and Rethlas-OSV. If I merely used AI to obtain a major result in a field unfamiliar to me and could not even understand the resulting paper, **I should not receive credit**.

If you are interested in **working through and organizing these results**, please contact me. I will provide more detailed materials, and **if you complete that work, the credit will be yours**. If you **find any errors**, please let me know; I will **make corrections and update the materials promptly**.
